title: The acceptance suite of conversations: written people carried from the first sentence to the holdout number
request: For each family, a written person run from the first sentence to the report, scored on the card, the workflow, the pipeline and the holdout number against the replica's planted truth; a gate fixed before the run; done when it passes on the sealed conversations with every family listed and its interval. Built ahead of 22.9, which is measured on it.
spec: A harness that plays each person as the product runs with no model, dev people written beside the rules, sealed people written apart and pinned, a fixed gate, and every product defect the dev failures show fixed in the product.
plan: Play one person through the coordinator to a built project.
Score the four parts against the replica's acceptance decisions.
Write a person per kind and fix the product where they fail.
Have the sealed people written apart, pin them, review, plant faults, run the sealed set once.

decisions.decision: The sealed people were written by a separate agent from a brief of the replicas, without the rules, the dev people or any code, and pinned before any run.
decisions.why: A set written beside the rules measured nothing in 20.2.

decisions.decision: The sealed run uses replica seed 1.
decisions.why: The dev failures were fixed on the seed 0 tables.

decisions.decision: Words for another family beside a named outcome column are asked, never inferred.
decisions.why: A word in passing must not refuse or redirect an ordinary project.

decisions.decision: A family the engine does not run is refused at the build and said as soon as it is known.
decisions.why: Built anyway it answered another question.

decisions.decision: Nothing is tuned on the sealed failures.
decisions.why: The set is spent; a fix judged on it would be judged by its own author.

change: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/journeys (new: the harness, dev people, the sealed people and their hash), evidence/campaigns/journeys_v1, kinds/acceptance.py (adopt), kinds/binary.py, kinds/__init__.py, studio/pipeline.py, studio/export.py, studio/code.py, agentic/routers/projects.py, draft/api.py, draft/card.py, draft/chat.py, dclab_core card.py, conversation.py, coordinator.py (dclab-core 0.32.0), Makefile; tests/test_journeys.py (new), test_pipeline.py, test_draft_flow.py, test_coordinator.py; the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.defect: The pipeline of every project built from a draft broke.
findings.scenario: Reading the pipeline of a draft-built project raised a validation error on the problem step.
findings.cause: The card keeps its family as a field with a value and a status; the step put the whole field where a word belongs, and the test used a made-up card.
findings.fix: The family is read as its value; the test builds a real card.

findings.defect: A yes or no outcome cleaned into booleans trained on one class without a word.
findings.scenario: The person's positive label yes matched no row of a column cleaning had turned into True and False; the leakage stage then failed on a metric it could not compute.
findings.cause: The label was compared as text with the table's booleans.
findings.fix: One helper reads yes as True on a boolean column, used by the engine, the Solution save and both exports; a label in no row, or in every row, is refused with the column's values.

findings.defect: A family the engine does not run was built as a model of one column.
findings.scenario: An uplift problem with a bought column was built and modelled as a response model, which answers another question.
findings.cause: No build check knew which families the engine runs.
findings.fix: The build refuses such a family with its rule, and the coordinator says so as soon as the family is known.

findings.defect: Blocks of places ran as a plain regression outside the maps pack.
findings.scenario: A flats table with coordinates under the tabular pack adopted blocks of places but ran as regression, not places.
findings.cause: The kind came from the pack alone.
findings.fix: A regression with blocks of places is the places kind under any pack.

findings.defect: A rare event's review budget was never asked.
findings.scenario: The fraud person answered four questions and the budget, which sets the rare-event metric, never came.
findings.cause: Home asked at most four of the pack's six fields.
findings.fix: Home asks at most five, the conversation gate's limit.

findings.defect: The words named no streams, entity tables or text, and missed common ways to say time to event and uplift.
findings.scenario: Raise an alert before a machine fails from its sensor readings was read as no family.
findings.cause: The card's word rules covered nine families.
findings.fix: Word rules for the three families and more wording for the two; beside a named outcome column they are asked, never inferred.

findings.defect: An outcome named inside a sentence was lost.
findings.scenario: days_subscribed, with cancelled saying whether they left was not read as the outcome.
findings.cause: Only an answer that was exactly a column counted.
findings.fix: An answer that begins with a column names it; columns are read in the order the answer names them.

findings.defect: An entity-tables outcome blocked the card.
findings.scenario: No order in the next 30 days was asked again as a column of the customers table.
findings.cause: With a table an outcome had to be a column.
findings.fix: For entity tables and streams the outcome in words counts, with a question to attach the table that decides it.

findings.defect: The refused-move check could never fire.
findings.scenario: Every transition counted as allowed, so the gate's no refused move clause was empty.
findings.cause: The harness read the list of open moves instead of the verdict's status.
findings.fix: Refused moves are the transitions whose status is blocked.

findings.defect: A family the engine does not run scored right on any stop.
findings.scenario: A ranking person who stopped at an unanswered question counted as refused.
findings.cause: Any stop with words was taken for the refusal.
findings.fix: Only a stop whose blocker is the refusal's rule counts.

findings.defect: The new build refusal blocked ordinary classification projects.
findings.scenario: Predict churn so we know who to target with retention calls, with a churned column, was refused as uplift.
findings.cause: A word rule settled the family against a named outcome column.
findings.fix: Words beside a named outcome column put both families in play and ask the person.

findings.defect: The new family words overrode a named outcome column and could open the card without one.
findings.scenario: Which customers will churn, from their tenure, plan and monthly charges read as entity tables.
findings.cause: The three new families sat ahead of the task's family.
findings.fix: Asked beside a named column; an outcome in words on one table says the table it needs.

findings.defect: A column only mentioned could become the outcome.
findings.scenario: We only know it once final_refund_amount is paid recorded the leak column as the target.
findings.cause: Any column name with an underscore counted wherever it sat.
findings.fix: Only an answer that begins with the column names it.

findings.defect: The exports read a yes label differently from the engine.
findings.scenario: On a cleaned boolean outcome the notebook export compared with yes and got all zeros.
findings.cause: The mapping lived in the engine only.
findings.fix: One helper, used by the save, the engine and both exports.

findings.defect: The harness saved the Solution without the validator.
findings.scenario: A save the product refuses could never show up in a journey.
findings.cause: The shared adopt step wrote the solution directly.
findings.fix: The journey saves through the graph's check and the column check, as the route; that path then found the route refusing a label file's target, fixed in the route.

findings.defect: The workflow part could not fail.
findings.scenario: Without a model the Home workflow is its template, valid by construction.
findings.cause: Only the Home workflow was checked.
findings.fix: 20.6's solution workflow is built from the problem card and the data card and validated on its content.

findings.defect: The gate did not require every family.
findings.scenario: A sealed set missing a family could pass.
findings.cause: Families were listed from the rows only.
findings.fix: Every family is listed, and one without a journey fails the gate.

findings.defect: The pipeline part accepted a step not recorded.
findings.scenario: A stage without its run record would have passed.
findings.cause: Not recorded counted as run.
findings.fix: Every step must be done; only the analysis of a kind with its own machine may be absent.

findings.defect: The holdout part did not say what the person stated, and ran on the dev tables.
findings.scenario: Five kinds were stated on the Solution page; the sealed run would read the tables the dev failures were fixed on.
findings.cause: The scoring did not check the kind, and one seed served both sets.
findings.fix: The problem must run as its kind, the row says whether the kind was stated, and the sealed run uses replica seed 1, fixed in the gate.

findings.defect: The sealed run could break on memory.
findings.scenario: Seven engines at once on an 8 GB machine could break the pool before anything was stored.
findings.cause: The default workers were all cores but one.
findings.fix: At most four by default.

findings.defect: A planted fault that took any stop for the refusal went unnoticed.
findings.scenario: The silent person failed on the card alone, so the test passed with the fault.
findings.cause: The test checked the whole row, not the refusal's part.
findings.fix: The test checks the refusal's part itself.

findings.defect: Every stage read as stale right after a full run.
findings.scenario: The pipeline compared runs made under the fast profile with the normal profile.
findings.cause: The engine profile is one of a run's inputs.
findings.fix: The harness reads the pipeline under the profile it ran with.

measurements.name: dev journeys
measurements.gate: journeys_gate_v1 read on dev: at least 85% right, interval lower end at least 0.6, every family, no refused move
measurements.result: 15 of 15 right on seed 0 and on seed 1, interval 0.796 to 1.0
limits: Written beside the rules: not evidence.

measurements.name: sealed journeys
measurements.gate: journeys_gate_v1 on the sealed set, run once on replica seed 1: at least 85% right, interval lower end at least 0.6, every family, no refused move
measurements.result: 16 of 30 right, interval 0.361 to 0.698, no refused move; right on all 12 classification, regression and segmentation journeys
limits: 30 people over seeded replicas, one writer.
The writer is a model instance, not a person.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 15 of 15 planted faults caught after one test was strengthened

outcome: The suite carries a written person from the first sentence to the holdout number the way the product runs, and found eight product defects on dev, all fixed; on the sealed people the rules reach the right card for the common families but not for people's own words for the others, and the gate fails.
lessons: A rule-read family fits the words it was written beside: the sealed people's own phrasings for the specialised families were missed in 11 of 14 misses.
A harness check that cannot fail must be found by planting the fault it should catch.
Saving through the product's own validator in a harness finds the product's bugs, not only the harness's.
risks: The card's family from people's own words needs the conversation reader or the person's statement.
A new sealed set needs an independent writer.
The kind's own fields are stated, not asked.
